thread.title: Robust Printing Business Makes Canon A Buy - Canon, Inc. (NYSE:CAJ)

author: Motek Moyen
title: Robust Printing Business Makes Canon A Buy - Canon, Inc. (NYSE:CAJ)
text:
All the prior Canon ( CAJ ) articles I published were all sell recommendations. I now endorse this camera and printer company as a buy. I am now convinced that Canon's printing business can offset the continuing decline in its imaging (camera and lenses) segment.
As per the FY 2018 report , the printing business posted a +16.7% Y/Y growth in operating profit. Canon is outperforming HP Inc. ( HPQ ) on printing and hard-copy peripherals. More importantly, the Japanese Canon is beating American HP Inc. inside the U.S. over sales of the A3 MFP (multifunction printer) category. This is very ironic since HP bought Samsung's ( OTC:SSNLF ) laser printer business in an attempt to take lead in the $55 billion/year A3 printer/copier industry.
(Source: IDC )
Judging by Canon outperforming HP Inc. inside America, I conclude that more American companies and individuals still believe that Japanese companies make the better cars and printers. A3 MFP and copiers are business-centric and Canon is no.1 in the U.S. American firms and business users clearly prefer Canon's printers to HP Inc. and Xerox's ( XRX ). This strong loyalty (or bias) of American customers toward the Canon brand is a Goliath buy signal for CAJ.
Why Long-Term Investors Should Consider CAJ Stop thinking Canon as a camera company. Think of it more as a printing company that is out boxing HP Inc. and Xerox in the U.S. market. Office (or the printing/ink supply business) is Canon's biggest revenue and profit generator. Its performance is, therefore, the more important gauge (for investing purposes) than Imaging (camera/lenses segment). The Office segment contributes 220.8 billion yen ($2.03 billion) to Canon's annual operating profit of 343 billion yen.
(Source: Canon)
The printing business is generating less than half of Canon's annual revenue and yet, it is responsible for more than 64% of operating profit.
CAJ is a buy because Canon's Imaging Systems segment is tanking but its Office (printing) and Medical System divisions are growing. Further, Canon still touts more than $4.72 billion in cash. Going forward, Canon can easily afford to buy smaller printing rivals Brother Industries ( OTCPK:BRTHY ) and Kyocera ( OTCPK:KYOCY ).
My fearless forecast is that Canon wants to catch up with HP Inc. on global printers & peripherals. Canon can do this easily if it gobbles up (or merge with) Brother and Kyocera. Consolidating its printing business with Brother and Kyocera will help Canon beat the leading consumer inkjet printing company, Epson ( OTCPK:SEKEY ).
Canon actually has a much bigger market share in global inkjet printers because of its leadership in office/business A4/A3 multifunction printers. Epson only leads in consumer-grade inkjet printers.
(Source: Statista)
Forget About The Paperless Office I understand that the global paperless office concept was just a mirage. HPQ, XRX, SEKEY, and CAJ are still posting growth in consumer and office printers. Corporate managers and home users know that important trade secrets/documents on hard-copy prints are still more secure than digital files or cloud-based documents.
Consider this scenario - the camera and printer trade secrets of Canon cannot easily be stolen/hacked by Chinese military people. Industrial espionage is now a more pervasive problem because of the internet. I suspect that Canon is hiding its design secrets on real paper documents, not on digital files. This is why no Chinese company has produced a competitive, professional-grade inkjet/laser printer or DSLR camera. If it were so, IDC would have listed a Chinese firm to be among the leaders in global printers and peripheral sales.
Chinese company Pantum has much cheaper but inferior A3 printers than what Canon offers. Unfortunately, security concerns again will still compel American and European companies to distrust a network and web-capable laser or inkjet printer made by a Chinese company.
Final Thoughts Canon's stock is cheap to own. CAJ's valuation ratios are very low based on Seeking Alpha's chart below. Any industry-leading company which has a P/S ratio of less than 1x (and a sub-20x P/E ratio) is a very sexy investment for me. Canon is no.2 in printing & peripherals and no.1 in professional cameras. Canon clearly deserves higher valuation ratios.
(Source: Seeking Alpha)
CAJ has upside potential when more large investors start treating it more as a printing company. Canon is really a hard-copy/printing company that just happened to be the long-time leader in the professional DSLR camera market/lenses industry.
I went long CAJ because I like the printing business. However, I cannot deny that Canon's long-term investment quality is also because of its invidious decades-old dominance in the DSLR camera market. Nikkei still reported that Canon has a 49.1% market share of the global 2018 interchangeable lens camera [ILC] or DSLR cameras industry. As of August 2018, there were 11.2 million (down 9% Y/Y) ILC cameras that were sold.
Pocket digital cameras are dead. However, the DSLR camera market dominated by Canon will not die even if Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) or Samsung comes up with better camera phones. No self-respecting photojournalist or wedding photographer is going to use an iPhone to do paid photography gigs. We clever photographers intimidate customers by touting our pricey Canon Camera DSLR cameras and lenses. In this way, we can demand higher professional fees.
We love our compact Fujifilm XT-2 mirrorless DSLR camera. Unfortunately, the phallic aura effect of having the biggest, longest lens attached to a Canon 7D or 6D seems to really excite potential wedding photography customers. Sad but true, the majority of customers still believe that heavy/bulky cameras with even very heavier lenses take better photos than mirrorless cameras.
My fearless forecast is that the resilient professional camera and lenses industry can keep Canon's Imaging System segment maintain its 1 trillion yen ($9.2 billion) annual revenue for the next five years. Canon's trusted brand makes it the no.1 choice for professional cameras and printers.
Canon has a captured customer base because it still sells professional cameras and expensive lenses that are not made in China (still made in Japan). Lastly, Canon was the last company to enter the mirrorless camera business and yet it is already no.1 in Japan. The November 2018 report of BCN also revealed that Canon is already no.2 in full-frame mirrorless camera shipments.
This is good because mirrorless camera sales are growing .
Disclosure: I am/we are long CAJ, AAPL, HPQ, SSNLF. it (other than from Seeking Alpha).
